The detector walks the repository (eight directories deep, at most 2,000 matching files, never following symbolic links) and skips dependency, build, and test-fixture directories:
Parsers treat contents as untrusted: input over a size limit yields nothing, line length and nesting are bounded, a malformed XML or properties file yields
declarations (not those read before the error), a
or entity declaration in a POM makes it unreadable, and nothing is evaluated.

Malformed: an unclosed XML tag, an entity declaration, unclosed Gradle calls, an empty or binary properties value, and pin files with no version. All must produce no findings and no crash.
The detector is quiet by default. A build that reads its JDK from a version catalog gets no lifecycle verdict from Offing, only an unclassified entry, which is the honest answer.
No rule says a Gradle or Kotlin version is unsupported. That gap is deliberate until their projects publish a lifecycle statement.
Relocated-dependency rules come from a candidate list checked against Maven Central by an importer, never from the scan.
